# Chapter Ten: Ghosts of the Father

> *"You can run to the end of the galaxy, but you can never outrun the blood running through your own veins."*

Hidden in the shadows of a decommissioned cargo hangar on New Tortuga's outer ring, *The Starlight Drifter* sat silent, its thrusters running on cold idle.

Tess sat cross-legged on the bridge floor, surrounded by holographic communication arrays. Her fingers flew across the keyboard as she intercepted wide-band subspace traffic from the core systems.

“Gracie,” Tess called quietly. “You need to hear this.”

Gracie stepped onto the bridge, a mug of bitter black coffee in her hands. “What is it?”

Tess tapped a command. A crackling, static-choked military broadcast filled the cockpit. The authoritative, battle-hardened voice sent a chill straight down Gracie’s spine.

*“—this is Captain Blake Campbell of the battlecruiser Revenant to all Union Ranger detachments in Sector 7. Hostile Shadow AI splinter fleets have broken through the Orion perimeter. Planetary defense shields on New Ceres have collapsed. We are engaging enemy dreadnoughts to cover civilian evacuation. Hold your positions. Campbell out.”*

The transmission cut out in a burst of harsh white noise.

Gracie stood frozen, her fingers tightening around the warm mug until the ceramic groaned.

*Your father,* the passenger’s voice rasped in her head. It was bitter, cold, and laced with years of cynical disillusionment. *The great hero. Always saving the galaxy. Where was he when Vengeance had me on the rack for a century? Where was he when Vengeance drilled into your skull? He didn't pull you out of that trash truck, Gracie. You saved yourself. Let him fight his war. We don't owe him a damn thing.*

Gracie closed her eyes, listening to the hum of *The Drifter*’s engines.

Every instinct in her urged her to agree. She had spent the last three months running, desperate to escape Blake’s shadow, terrified of being seen as weak or broken.

“He’s losing that sector,” Kael said quietly, standing in the doorway of the bridge. “If the Shadow AI swarms break through Sector 7, New Tortuga and every free colony in the Orion Belt will be wiped off the map.”

Gracie looked at the glowing sapphire Aegis Core resting securely in the auxiliary manifold.

“I spent my whole life thinking I had to either be Blake Campbell's perfect soldier or a runaway ghost,” Gracie murmured, her voice steadying. “Vengeance tried to turn me into a broken toy. But I didn't crawl out of that garbage chute just to hide in the dark while people burn.”

*What are you saying?* the passenger asked, nervous apprehension creeping back into its tone.

“I’m saying my father can fight his war,” Gracie said, setting her mug down on the console and grabbing the flight controls. “And we’re going to fight ours.”
